findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When an override exists for the slot's date, this function returns true before checking `busy`. Overrides specify working availability, not freedom from bookings or calendar events. A host with a 10:00–12:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking will therefore be advertised as available at 10:00. Continue through the busy-time checks after validating the override.

findings.title: Split working hours reject slots inside either valid interval
findings.body: The new working-hours check rejects a slot if it is outside any interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it fits at least one interval. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon interval, and afternoon slots are rejected because they are outside the morning interval. This can remove all availability for split schedules.

findings.title: Override validation accepts partially overlapping slots
findings.body: The override check only rejects slots that end before the override starts or start after it ends. It does not require the full event to fit inside the override. In a round-robin event, slots generated from another host's availability can therefore pass a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override even when they run 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 (or start exactly at 11:00). Require slot start >= override start and slot end <= override end.

findings.title: Multiple override intervals are treated as simultaneous constraints
findings.body: Using `find` to reject a slot outside any override interval makes multiple intervals on the same date mutually exclusive. With overrides 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, a morning slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and an afternoon slot by the morning interval. Check whether the slot fits any interval on the override date instead of rejecting it based on another interval.
